intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under the famous weeping cherry tree in Kyoto's most celebrated public park. Join locals for picnics, lantern-lit evening strolls, and stunning pink blossom canopies. Family-friendly with open spaces for children to play.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the Thunder Gate and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional snacks, souvenirs, and crafts. Highly engaging for families with rich historical storytelling and colorful surroundings.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling outer market of the world-famous Tsukiji fish market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette), matcha sweets, and street skewers from local vendors. A delicious deep-dive into Japanese culinary culture that kids and adults alike will love.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, this UNESCO World Heritage Site includes the iconic A-Bomb Dome and the Peace Memorial Museum. Learn about the history of World War II and Japan's message of peace and resilience. Suitable for children aged 10 and above with guided family tours available.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama and then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Stunning natural scenery combined with a unique wildlife encounter makes this a perfect family adventure. Cherry blossom trees line the nearby Oi River in spring.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and exchange currency at the airport for better rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the airport limousine bus or train to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, beachfront area). Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along the nearby beachfront promenade to get your bearings. Enjoy the coastal scenery and spot any cherry blossom trees in bloom along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local neighborhood on foot. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, or Lawson) to stock up on budget-friendly snacks and drinks. Enjoy a casual dinner at a local ramen or gyudon (beef bowl) chain restaurant near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal or airport snack
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store onigiri and drinks (~¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya or Sukiya gyudon chain restaurant near hotel (~¥500–¥700)

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize rest after the flight. Set up a Suica or IC card at the station for easy public transport payments throughout the trip. April mid-month is peak cherry blossom season — expect crowds at popular spots.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the nearest local shrine or temple in the morning. Many Japanese coastal towns have historic shrines with beautiful torii gates and cherry blossom trees on the grounds. Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) to enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before crowds arrive. Admission is typically free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby traditional fishing village or historic district on foot or by local bus. Look for preserved Edo-period architecture, local craft shops, and small museums (entry fees usually ¥200–¥500). Pick up a local culture map from the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant) for an affordable dinner. Order shared small plates like edamame, karaage (fried chicken), and yakitori skewers. A filling meal for two can cost ¥1,500–¥2,500 total.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or convenience store egg sandwich and green tea (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Local soba or udon noodle shop (~¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Neighborhood izakaya with small plates and drinks (~¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Many shrines and temples are free to enter — donations are optional. Check local tourism boards for free cultural events happening this week.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hanami (cherry blossom viewing) picnic at the nearest public park. Buy bento boxes and drinks from a convenience store the night before to save money. Arrive early to claim a good spot under the blooming sakura trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local history museum or cultural heritage center. Many municipal museums in Japan charge very low entry fees (¥100–¥300) or are completely free. Learn about the region's history through exhibits on traditional crafts, local festivals, and historical artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through a covered shopping arcade (shotengai) in the nearest town center. Browse 100-yen shops (Daiso) for souvenirs and household items. Grab dinner at a kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant where plates start from ¥100–¥130 each.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri, boiled egg, and miso soup cup (~¥350–¥500)
meals.lunch: Picnic bento box from convenience store under the cherry blossoms (~¥500–¥700)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi conveyor belt sushi (~¥800–¥1,200 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a picnic mat or blanket for the hanami. April cherry blossoms are weather-dependent — check local bloom forecasts. Daiso 100-yen shops are excellent for budget souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by local train or bus to the nearest major historical city or castle town. Arrive early to beat tourist crowds at the castle grounds. Many Japanese castles charge ¥300–¥600 entry and offer panoramic views of the surrounding area and cherry blossom trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the castle town's historic samurai district or old merchant quarter. Many preserved streetscapes are free to walk through. Visit a small local craft workshop where artisans demonstrate traditional skills like pottery, lacquerware, or weaving (free or low-cost to observe).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area by early evening. Dine at a teishoku (set meal) restaurant offering a full meal with rice, miso soup, pickles, and a main dish for ¥700–¥1,000.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Castle town local restaurant — try regional specialty dishes (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal restaurant near hotel (~¥700–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Research train or bus schedules the night before. IC card (Suica) makes ticketing seamless. Many castle grounds have free outer gardens even if the main keep charges admission.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Buddhist temple complex in the morning. Walk the temple grounds, observe morning prayers if permitted, and explore the cemetery gardens which often feature beautiful stone lanterns and moss-covered paths. Free entry at most temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a free or low-cost cultural experience — look for public calligraphy demonstrations, ikebana (flower arranging) displays, or tea ceremony introductions at community centers or tourist information offices (~¥500–¥1,000 for guided tea ceremony).
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from a local supermarket (visit in the evening for discounted bento boxes marked down 20–50%). This is a great budget strategy — look for orange discount stickers on prepared foods.

meals.breakfast: Japanese-style hotel breakfast or convenience store (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Temple district tofu restaurant or vegetarian Buddhist cuisine (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Discounted supermarket bento boxes and side dishes (~¥400–¥700)

day_by_day.notes: Supermarkets typically discount prepared foods after 7:00–8:00 PM. This is one of the best budget travel hacks in Japan. Many community centers offer free cultural demonstrations — ask at the hotel or tourist office.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the beachfront area near the hotel. Take an early morning walk along the shore to enjoy the sunrise and coastal scenery. Look for local fishing boats returning with the morning catch — this is a uniquely Japanese coastal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fish market or morning market (ichiba). Sample fresh seafood, local produce, and regional snacks. Many coastal markets have affordable fresh seafood bowls (kaisendon) for ¥800–¥1,500 — excellent value for the quality.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor cultural event, lantern festival, or community gathering if available in the area (April often features spring festivals). Otherwise, enjoy a scenic evening walk along the illuminated beachfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood kaisendon (rice bowl) at the fish market (~¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Local tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant or family restaurant chain (~¥700–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check local event calendars for spring matsuri (festivals) — many are free to attend. Coastal fish markets are typically most active in the early morning (6:00–9:00 AM).

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer day trip by regional train to a famous cherry blossom viewing spot or historic town in the wider region. Research UNESCO World Heritage sites or nationally designated scenic spots within 1–2 hours of your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day trip destination thoroughly — visit the main historical attraction, walk through traditional streets, and browse local craft shops. Look for free public parks, shrines, and viewpoints to maximize the experience without spending heavily.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by early evening. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to mark the halfway point of the trip — try a local specialty restaurant featuring the region's signature dish (~¥1,200–¥2,000).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before catching the train (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Local specialty restaurant at the day trip destination (~¥900–¥1,300)
meals.dinner: Regional specialty restaurant near hotel — a small splurge (~¥1,200–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Buy round-trip train tickets in advance if possible. Use the IC card for seamless transfers. Day 7 is a good time for a small budget splurge on dinner as a halfway celebration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Shinto shrine known for family blessings and good fortune (many coastal shrines are dedicated to safe seafaring and family protection). Participate in drawing an omikuji (fortune slip) for ¥100–¥200 — a fun cultural tradition for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a hands-on cultural workshop — look for local pottery studios, indigo dyeing workshops, or traditional paper (washi) making classes. Many tourist areas offer beginner workshops for ¥500–¥1,500 per person, and you get to take home a handmade souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing onsen (hot spring bath) experience if available near your hotel. Many public sento bathhouses charge only ¥400–¥500 per person. This is an authentic Japanese cultural experience perfect for families.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Curry rice at a CoCo Ichibanya chain or local curry restaurant (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewer restaurant or standing ramen bar (~¥600–¥900)

day_by_day.notes: Omikuji fortunes are a beloved Japanese tradition — tie bad fortunes to the shrine's designated rack to leave the bad luck behind. Check onsen rules: tattoos may be restricted at some facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to souvenir shopping at budget-friendly spots — 100-yen shops, local markets, and supermarkets for regional food products (mochi, matcha sweets, soy sauce, etc.) make excellent affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Revisit your favorite spot from the trip for a final, leisurely exploration. Take photos, sit in a cherry blossom park, or simply enjoy the atmosphere of a place that resonated with you. Reflect on the cultural experiences of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a nicer local restaurant to celebrate the end of the trip. Choose a place serving a regional specialty you haven't tried yet — kaiseki-lite set meals or a quality sushi restaurant offer good value at ¥1,500–¥2,500.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Standing sushi bar or soba restaurant (~¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local specialty restaurant (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — Japanese packaging is often beautiful but fragile. Supermarket regional food products are some of the best value souvenirs in Japan. Confirm departure logistics for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk along the beachfront near the hotel — take in the scenery one last time and enjoy a quiet breakfast. Check out of the hotel and store luggage if needed for a few extra hours of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, make a final stop at a nearby convenience store for travel snacks and drinks for the journey home. Visit any last-minute sights near the airport or transit hub. Return any rented items (IC card deposit refund at station machines).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Japan with wonderful memories. Use remaining yen for airport shopping — duty-free shops offer good deals on Japanese cosmetics, snacks, and whisky. Board flight home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store final Japanese breakfast (~¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Airport food court — try a final bowl of ramen or soba (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant before departure

day_by_day.notes: Refund your IC card (Suica) balance and deposit at any major station before heading to the airport. Keep ¥3,000–¥5,000 in cash for airport transport and last-minute purchases. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under the famous weeping cherry tree in Kyoto's most celebrated public park. Join locals for picnics, lantern-lit evening strolls, and stunning pink blossom canopies. Family-friendly with open spaces for children to play.

Highly engaging for families with rich historical storytelling and colorful surroundings.

experiences.description: Explore the bustling outer market of the world-famous Tsukiji fish market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette), matcha sweets, and street skewers from local vendors. A delicious deep-dive into Japanese culinary culture that kids and adults alike will love.

experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama and then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Stunning natural scenery combined with a unique wildlife encounter makes this a perfect family adventure. Cherry blossom trees line the nearby Oi River in spring.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-in — Flight lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the nearby beachfront promenade to acclimate to Japan. Visit a local convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) to pick up snacks and essentials — a quintessential Japanese experience in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first-night dinner near the hotel. Explore the local neighborhood, find a welcoming izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant) for a relaxed introduction to Japanese cuisine with grilled skewers, edamame, and cold Asahi beer.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store onigiri and bento box — budget-friendly and authentically Japanese
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the resort — try yakitori skewers, miso soup, and cold tofu. Expect ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is real — keep Day 1 light and low-stress. Set your watch to Japan Standard Time immediately. Purchase a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. April 15 typically falls within peak cherry blossom season, so expect crowds at popular spots.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street — Head to Asakusa early (arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Visit Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple dating to 628 AD. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), stroll Nakamise-dori lined with traditional craft shops, and offer a prayer at the main hall. The surrounding Asakusa district is rich in old Edo atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the temple, explore the Sumida River waterfront where cherry blossom trees line the banks — a perfect hanami moment. Cross to the modern Skytree area for contrast. Visit the Sumida Park cherry blossom promenade and enjoy a picnic-style hanami lunch on the grass.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward central Tokyo. Visit Ueno Park at dusk for magical illuminated cherry blossoms (yozakura). The park hosts one of Tokyo's most famous hanami festivals in April. Grab street food from festival stalls — yakisoba, taiyaki, and candied strawberries.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) — try morning toast set with egg and coffee for ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Picnic-style hanami lunch from Asakusa's Nakamise stalls — ningyo-yaki (sweet cakes), senbei (rice crackers), and onigiri. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Ueno area ramen shop — try a hearty tonkotsu or shoyu ramen bowl. Budget ¥900–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll log 8–12 km today. Senso-ji is free to enter. Bring a small backpack for shopping finds on Nakamise-dori. Cherry blossoms in mid-April may be slightly past peak in Tokyo but still beautiful, especially along the Sumida River.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Arrive at Tsukiji Outer Market by 8:00 AM for the freshest experience. The outer market (open to the public) is a vibrant maze of seafood vendors, egg vendors, and street food stalls. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and uni (sea urchin) on toast. This is a world-class culinary adventure for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tsukiji, walk or take a short taxi to Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, teahouse, and incredible cherry blossom trees. Enjoy matcha tea and wagashi (traditional sweets) at the garden teahouse overlooking the water. Afterwards, take the waterbus up the Sumida River for scenic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Odaiba waterfront district for a family-friendly evening. Visit the teamLab Planets or Odaiba shopping malls, enjoy views of Rainbow Bridge illuminated at night, and dine with a Tokyo skyline backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market grazing — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and green tea. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person for a satisfying market breakfast
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse — matcha and wagashi set (¥800), plus a light bento from a nearby convenience store
meals.dinner: Odaiba — try a mid-range Japanese family restaurant (family resto) such as Gusto or a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) for a fun, interactive dinner. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest on weekends — arrive early to avoid the worst crowds. The inner market (tuna auctions) has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains a must-visit. Hamarikyu Gardens entry fee is ¥300 per adult. The waterbus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa is a scenic and practical way to travel (¥780 per adult).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa (about 2 hours, ¥1,360 each way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex, one of Japan's most elaborately decorated shrines dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu. Spot the famous 'See No Evil, Hear No Evil, Speak No Evil' monkeys carved above the stable. The surrounding cedar forest is majestic and serene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's sacred grounds — visit Rinnoji Temple and the Futarasan Shrine. Walk along the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. If time permits, take a short bus ride to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls, and Lake Chuzenji for mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (aim to board the 17:00–18:00 train). Have a quiet dinner near the hotel to rest after a full day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or convenience store before catching the train
meals.lunch: Nikko town restaurants — try yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty. Look for a set lunch at a local restaurant near the shrine. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Neighborhood restaurant near the resort — try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set meal. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass (¥4,780) for unlimited buses within Nikko and discounted train fare — excellent value for a full day. Wear layers as Nikko's mountain elevation can be cooler than Tokyo. The Tosho-gu complex entry is ¥1,300 per adult. Book the train tickets the night before to secure seats on busy Sunday trains.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Tokyo to Kyoto via Shinkansen (Nozomi, approx. 2 hours 15 minutes, ¥13,870 per person). Arrive in Kyoto by mid-morning. Check luggage at the hotel or use coin lockers at Kyoto Station. Begin with a visit to Nijo Castle — the former Kyoto residence of the Tokugawa shoguns, famous for its 'nightingale floors' that squeak to alert guards of intruders. A wonderful history lesson for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — the iconic path of thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mount Inari. You can hike as far as you like; even the first 30–45 minutes offers breathtaking photo opportunities. The trail is free and open at all hours.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Gion district at dusk — Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Walk along Hanamikoji Street and Shirakawa Canal lined with cherry blossom trees and traditional machiya townhouses. If lucky, spot a geiko (geisha) or maiko (apprentice) heading to an evening engagement.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen ekiben (station bento box) purchased at Tokyo Station — a delightful travel tradition. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Near Fushimi Inari — try inari-zushi (sushi rice in tofu pockets, named after the shrine's fox deity) from a local stall. Budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Gion area kaiseki-lite set meal or a tofu-cuisine restaurant — Kyoto is famous for refined tofu dishes. Try a mid-range kaiseki set for ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance, especially for April travel during cherry blossom season — trains fill quickly. Fushimi Inari is free to enter and most magical in early morning or evening when crowds thin. The Gion district has strict photography rules to protect residents' privacy — be respectful and avoid pointing cameras at geiko or maiko.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park — Take the JR Sagano Line to Arashiyama (20 minutes from Kyoto Station). Walk through the ethereal bamboo grove in the morning light — the towering green stalks create an otherworldly atmosphere. Then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (20-minute uphill trail) where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Kids will love it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the broader Arashiyama area — visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden, one of Kyoto's finest Zen gardens. Stroll along the Oi River and rent a rowboat for 30 minutes (¥1,500–¥2,000 per boat). Cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge framed by cherry blossoms and mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — a narrow 400-meter covered arcade with over 100 stalls selling pickles, tofu, fresh seafood, and Kyoto specialties. Perfect for grazing and souvenir shopping before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local Kyoto-style morning set at a kissaten near the accommodation
meals.lunch: Arashiyama riverside restaurant — try a yudofu (hot tofu) set lunch or soba noodles with mountain vegetable tempura. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market area — try a mix of small plates from market stalls (kushi katsu, Kyoto pickles, fresh mochi) followed by dinner at a nearby ramen or udon shop. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is free to walk through but gets crowded after 9:00 AM — aim to arrive by 8:00 AM. Iwatayama Monkey Park entry is ¥600 per adult, ¥300 per child. Tenryu-ji garden entry is ¥500. Do not feed the monkeys outside the designated feeding area. The rowboats are a family highlight — book or queue early as they sell out.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing at Maruyama Park — Visit Kyoto's most famous hanami spot, centered around the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) that is hundreds of years old. Mid-April may catch the tail end of blossoms but the atmosphere is magical. Stroll through the park and neighboring Yasaka Shrine, which dates to 656 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Higashiyama Historic District — a beautifully preserved hillside neighborhood of traditional machiya townhouses, stone-paved lanes, and craft shops. Walk the Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka (Two-Year Slope and Three-Year Slope) pathways leading to Kiyomizudera Temple, one of Japan's most celebrated temples with its famous wooden stage jutting out over the hillside.
day_by_day.evening: Kiyomizudera offers special evening illuminations in April (check dates) — the temple and surrounding cherry trees are lit up magnificently after dark. Return to Gion for a well-deserved farewell Kyoto dinner.

meals.breakfast: Maruyama Park area — pick up a fresh coffee and pastry from a local café before the park opens fully
meals.lunch: Higashiyama district — try a matcha parfait and light lunch at one of the many charming teahouses along Ninenzaka. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Gion district — a mid-range kaiseki restaurant or a modern Japanese fusion restaurant. Try a 5-course kaiseki set for ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person — a splurge-worthy final Kyoto dinner

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free to enter. Kiyomizudera entry is ¥500 per adult. Evening illuminations at Kiyomizudera typically run from sunset to 21:00 during cherry blossom season — verify the schedule upon arrival in Kyoto. Wear comfortable shoes as Higashiyama involves a lot of uphill walking on stone paths. The Sannenzaka is said to bring bad luck if you stumble — watch your step!

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima — Take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approx. 1 hour, ¥10,800 per person on the Sakura or Hikari service). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and essential experience for families. The museum chronicles the atomic bombing of August 6, 1945, with remarkable sensitivity and historical depth. The Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Peace Memorial Park, visiting the Children's Peace Monument (inspired by Sadako Sasaki's story of paper cranes), the Flame of Peace, and the Memorial Cenotaph. Then take the tram or ferry to Miyajima Island — visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine with its 'floating' torii gate rising from the sea. Wander the island and encounter friendly wild deer roaming freely.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city for dinner before catching the Shinkansen back to Kyoto (last trains run until around 22:00). Hiroshima is famous for its own style of okonomiyaki — a must-try.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or onigiri from a convenience store before catching the Shinkansen
meals.lunch: Hiroshima city near the Peace Park — try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered savory pancake with noodles, cabbage, and egg) at Okonomimura, a multi-floor building of okonomiyaki restaurants. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Hiroshima station area or near the Peace Park — try oysters (Hiroshima produces 60% of Japan's oysters) grilled, fried, or in a hot pot. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum (¥200 per adult) is deeply emotional — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. Allow at least 2 hours for the museum. The ferry to Miyajima departs from Hiroshima Port or Miyajimaguchi (JR Pass covers the JR ferry). The floating torii gate is best seen at high tide — check tide tables in advance. This is one of the most historically significant days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Kyoto to Tokyo via Shinkansen (if returning to base) OR a final morning in Kyoto visiting the Philosopher's Path — a 2 km stone walkway along a canal lined with hundreds of cherry trees, connecting Nanzenji Temple to Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion). One of Kyoto's most romantic and peaceful walks, especially in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion) and its stunning Zen garden with the famous 'Sea of Silver Sand' and 'Moon Viewing Platform.' Then head to the Heian Shrine, built in 1895 to commemorate Kyoto's 1,100th anniversary — its garden features extraordinary weeping cherry trees. Begin making your way toward your final destination or back toward the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Kyoto dinner or arrival back at the resort area for a relaxed beachfront evening. If back at the resort, enjoy a sunset walk along the beach and a casual seafood dinner to wind down.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up for a walking-heavy morning
meals.lunch: Philosopher's Path area — try a charming café lunch with homemade tofu or vegetable curry near Nanzenji Temple. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Resort area beachfront seafood restaurant — try grilled fish, tempura, and miso soup with a view. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ginkakuji entry is ¥500 per adult. Heian Shrine garden entry is ¥600 per adult. The Philosopher's Path is free and most beautiful in early morning. If traveling back to Tokyo by Shinkansen, book the afternoon train to arrive by early evening. This day offers a beautiful balance of reflection and relaxation before the final day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort and a final walk along the beachfront. Pack souvenirs carefully. Visit a nearby shopping area for last-minute gifts: Japanese Kit Kats in regional flavors, matcha sweets, tenugui (traditional cloth), and sake make wonderful gifts. If near Tokyo, the Shibuya or Shinjuku department store basement floors (depachika) are paradise for food souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight timing — if afternoon/evening flight, head to the airport with ample time (arrive 3 hours before international departure). Use remaining Suica card balance on airport train or snacks. If no flight today, spend a final relaxed afternoon at the resort pool or beach, reflecting on an incredible 10 days in Japan.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final resort evening. Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner — try a Japanese steakhouse (teppanyaki) for a theatrical and memorable final meal, with a chef cooking Wagyu beef, seafood, and vegetables on an iron griddle before you.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — make it a leisurely, special final morning meal
meals.lunch: Airport or shopping district — a final bowl of ramen or a sushi conveyor belt lunch. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki farewell dinner — Wagyu beef set course with miso soup, rice, and seasonal vegetables. Budget ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person (a well-earned splurge on the final night)

day_by_day.notes: Japan's consumption tax (currently 10%) is included in displayed prices. Keep all receipts — tourists can claim tax-free shopping (8% refund) at participating stores with a passport. Make sure to spend or transfer remaining Suica card balance before leaving (it can be refunded at major stations for a ¥220 fee). Carry your passport for tax-free shopping. Sayonara and arigato gozaimashita — Japan will be missed!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under the famous weeping cherry tree in Kyoto's most celebrated public park. Join locals for picnics, lantern-lit evening strolls, and stunning pink blossom canopies. Family-friendly with open spaces for children to play.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the Thunder Gate and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional snacks, souvenirs, and crafts. Highly engaging for families with rich historical storytelling and colorful surroundings.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling outer market of the world-famous Tsukiji fish market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette), matcha sweets, and street skewers from local vendors. A delicious deep-dive into Japanese culinary culture that kids and adults alike will love.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, this UNESCO World Heritage Site includes the iconic A-Bomb Dome and the Peace Memorial Museum. Learn about the history of World War II and Japan's message of peace and resilience. Suitable for children aged 10 and above with guided family tours available.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama and then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Stunning natural scenery combined with a unique wildlife encounter makes this a perfect family adventure. Cherry blossom trees line the nearby Oi River in spring.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00; no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury car transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront suite and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Leisure — Explore the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds, enjoy the beachfront terrace, and unwind after the long flight. Visit the resort's concierge to confirm upcoming bookings and receive a curated welcome briefing on Japan etiquette and highlights.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner at the Resort — Enjoy a private kaiseki (traditional multi-course Japanese) dinner at the resort's signature restaurant, featuring seasonal spring ingredients and locally sourced seafood.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at the airport lounge or en route to the resort
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — omakase tasting menu with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: No activities before 13:00 arrival. Request early check-in in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed to combat jet lag. Ask concierge for next-day wake-up call and restaurant reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street — Take a private guided tour to Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple (628 AD). Arrive early to beat crowds, explore the Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, the five-story pagoda, and the main hall. Walk the historic Nakamise shopping arcade for premium souvenirs and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Join a private gourmet food tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), wagyu skewers, and seasonal street foods. Learn about Japan's legendary seafood culture from a local expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Dinner in Ginza — Head to Ginza, Tokyo's most prestigious dining district, for dinner at a Michelin-starred sushi restaurant. Enjoy an intimate omakase counter experience with the freshest seasonal fish.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast buffet at the resort — miso soup, grilled fish, rice, pickles, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Gourmet tastings during the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — fresh uni, otoro sashimi, and artisan snacks
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at a Michelin-starred sushi restaurant in Ginza (e.g., Sushi Yoshitake or equivalent) — premium sake pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Book Senso-ji private guide and Ginza restaurant well in advance. Arrive at Tsukiji by midday for the best vendor selection. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — Travel to Kyoto's Arashiyama district for a serene early-morning walk through the iconic bamboo grove before crowds arrive. Hire a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) for a scenic ride through the historic lanes of Sagano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Iwatayama Monkey Park — Hike up to the Arashiyama Monkey Park for a family-friendly encounter with wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Afterwards, explore the nearby Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Kyoto Dinner in Gion — Dine at a premium kaiseki restaurant in the historic Gion district. Opt for a private room (zashiki) experience with floor seating and a geisha or maiko performance if available.

meals.breakfast: Continental and Japanese breakfast at the resort before early departure
meals.lunch: Bento box lunch at a riverside café in Arashiyama overlooking the Oi River
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner in Gion (e.g., Kikunoi Honten or equivalent) — seasonal spring menu featuring bamboo shoots and cherry blossom-themed dishes

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (by 7:00 AM) to reach Arashiyama before tourist crowds. Tenryu-ji garden entry fee required. Check availability of ozashiki (geisha dinner) experiences through your concierge — these book months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing at Maruyama Park — Experience the iconic hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) in Maruyama Park. Arrive early for a peaceful stroll and family photos. A private guide will explain the cultural significance of cherry blossoms in Japanese history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kyoto Imperial Palace & Nijo Castle — Visit the Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds and the nearby Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its 'nightingale floors' and stunning Ninomaru Palace interiors. A private guide brings the feudal history to life.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Cocktails & Fine Dining — Enjoy sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Kyoto skyline, followed by dinner at a contemporary Japanese restaurant blending traditional Kyoto cuisine (kyo-ryori) with modern techniques.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at a traditional Kyoto café — tofu dishes, yudofu, and matcha
meals.lunch: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) lunch near Maruyama Park — a unique and historically rich dining experience
meals.dinner: Contemporary kyo-ryori dinner at a premium Kyoto restaurant (e.g., Hyotei or equivalent) — wine and sake pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom peak in mid-April is ideal — confirm bloom status closer to the date. Nijo Castle requires advance ticket booking. The nightingale floor corridors are a highlight for children.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Explore the world-famous vermillion torii gate tunnels of Fushimi Inari early in the morning. Hike the lower trails for stunning views and atmospheric forest paths. A private guide explains the Shinto fox deity (kitsune) mythology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Kyoto Artisan Workshops — Walk through Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') sampling premium street foods. Participate in a private Japanese cultural workshop — choose from matcha tea ceremony, wagashi (sweet-making), or ikebana (flower arranging).
day_by_day.evening: Private Dinner Cruise or Riverside Kaiseki — Enjoy a private dinner along the Kamo River at a premier riverside restaurant with an open-air engawa (veranda) terrace, ideal for a romantic and family-friendly evening under the spring sky.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before the shrine visit
meals.lunch: Gourmet tastings at Nishiki Market — fresh tofu, pickled vegetables, grilled skewers, and matcha soft serve
meals.dinner: Riverside kaiseki dinner at a top Kyoto restaurant (e.g., Mizai or Kichisen) — full seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is best visited before 8:00 AM to avoid crowds. Wear comfortable shoes for the torii trail hike. Cultural workshop bookings should be arranged through the concierge at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & Park — Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) to Hiroshima for a deeply moving and educational family experience. Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Peace Memorial Park, the Atomic Bomb Dome, and the Peace Memorial Museum. A private guide provides historical context appropriate for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island & Itsukushima Shrine — Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high tide. Stroll the island's scenic paths, encounter friendly deer, and visit the five-story pagoda.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Resort & Relaxing Dinner — Return by Shinkansen and private transfer. Enjoy a quieter, reflective evening with a premium dinner at the resort or a nearby fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at the resort before Shinkansen departure
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory pancake) lunch at a renowned local restaurant — a regional specialty not to be missed
meals.dinner: Light but luxurious seafood dinner at the resort restaurant — grilled oysters (Hiroshima is famous for them) and seasonal sashimi

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum contains graphic historical content — review age-appropriateness for younger children in advance. The floating torii is most dramatic at high tide — check tide schedules. Book Shinkansen tickets in advance via your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Nara Day Trip — Travel to Nara, Japan's ancient capital, for a morning of history and wildlife. Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue, and walk through Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming deer bow for shika senbei (deer crackers).
day_by_day.afternoon: Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine & Isuien Garden — Explore the ancient Kasuga Taisha Shrine, one of Japan's most sacred Shinto sites, lined with thousands of stone and bronze lanterns. Visit the serene Isuien Garden for a meditative stroll through one of Japan's finest stroll gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Sake Tasting & Gourmet Dinner — Return to the resort area and visit a premium sake brewery or tasting bar for a guided sake pairing experience. Follow with dinner at a high-end restaurant specializing in Yamato cuisine (ancient Nara-style Japanese cooking).

meals.breakfast: Full Japanese breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Kaiseki bento lunch at a traditional Nara restaurant near Isuien Garden
meals.dinner: Yamato cuisine tasting menu at a premium Nara or resort-area restaurant — sake flight pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Deer in Nara Park are wild — supervise young children. Todai-ji is busiest midday; arrive early. Kasuga Taisha's lantern-lighting ceremonies (held in February and August) are legendary — check for any special spring events.

day_by_day.morning: Osaka Castle & History Walk — Visit the magnificent Osaka Castle, one of Japan's most iconic landmarks. Explore the museum inside the main tower detailing the castle's role in Japan's unification. Stroll through the surrounding park with cherry blossoms still in late bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dotonbori & Kuromon Ichiba Market — Explore Osaka's vibrant Dotonbori entertainment district. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market ('Osaka's Kitchen') for premium tastings of fresh seafood, wagyu beef, and street delicacies. A private food guide leads the culinary adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Osaka Fine Dining — Experience Osaka's legendary 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop) culture at its finest. Dine at a Michelin-starred restaurant in the Kitashinchi dining district, Osaka's most prestigious culinary neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel-style breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet street food tastings at Kuromon Ichiba — fresh crab, wagyu skewers, and takoyaki (octopus balls) from premium vendors
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred dinner in Kitashinchi, Osaka (e.g., Fujiya 1935 or equivalent) — innovative Japanese cuisine with French influences

day_by_day.notes: Osaka Castle can be crowded on weekends — consider a private after-hours tour if available. Dotonbori is lively and family-friendly in the afternoon. The Glico Running Man sign is a classic photo opportunity.

day_by_day.morning: Hakone — Mt. Fuji Views & Ryokan Experience — Travel to Hakone for Japan's most iconic natural scenery. Board the Hakone Ropeway for aerial views of Mt. Fuji (weather permitting) and the volcanic Owakudani valley. Visit Hakone Open Air Museum for a family-friendly blend of art and nature.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lake Ashi Cruise & Hakone Shrine — Cruise across the serene Lake Ashi on a replica pirate galleon for panoramic views of Mt. Fuji framed by cherry blossoms. Visit the lakeside Hakone Shrine with its torii gate rising from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Ryokan Dinner & Onsen — Check into a premium ryokan (traditional Japanese inn) for the night. Enjoy a private multi-course kaiseki dinner in your room served by a personal attendant, followed by a soak in the natural hot spring onsen bath.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Soba noodle lunch at a traditional Hakone restaurant with Mt. Fuji views
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki dinner at the ryokan — 10-course seasonal tasting menu with local Hakone spring water-brewed sake

day_by_day.notes: Mt. Fuji visibility depends on weather and cloud cover — morning views are typically clearest. Ryokan etiquette: remove shoes at the entrance, wear provided yukata robes. Onsen has separate bathing hours for families vs. adults — confirm with ryokan. Book the ryokan well in advance as premium rooms sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Onsen & Ryokan Farewell Breakfast — Wake early for a private sunrise soak in the outdoor rotenburo (open-air onsen) with views of Mt. Fuji at dawn — an unforgettable final morning. Enjoy a traditional Japanese breakfast at the ryokan: grilled fish, miso soup, rice, pickles, and fresh tofu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return Journey & Final Shopping — Travel back toward the resort or airport area. Stop at a premium department store (e.g., Isetan or Takashimaya) for last-minute luxury Japanese gift shopping — premium teas, wagashi, lacquerware, and textiles. Return to the resort for final packing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gala Dinner — Celebrate the final evening with a grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant or a nearby top-rated establishment. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days with a champagne toast and a curated menu of Japan's greatest culinary highlights.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the ryokan — the quintessential final morning meal
meals.lunch: Premium bento box or light lunch at a department store food hall (depachika) — a world-class Japanese culinary experience in itself
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant or a nearby Michelin-starred venue — champagne, wagyu, seasonal seafood, and a dessert platter celebrating Japanese spring flavors

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout at the ryokan to maximize the morning onsen experience. Depachika (department store basement food halls) are excellent for high-quality omiyage (souvenir gifts). Confirm departure logistics with the concierge — private airport transfer should be arranged in advance. Allow at least 3 hours before any evening or next-day flight.
